purpose: Pins the one buildx executable that a CAP release-equivalent build is allowed to run, so that producer identity does not depend on which plugin a GitHub runner happens to have installed. Batch 3 A2.1 established it in the non-publishing observation job; A2.2 put the publishing path on it too.
why_not_the_release_lock: deployment/third-party-images.json is the lock the shipped deployment reads (F-20), and the diff classifier treats anything under deployment/ as runtime-affecting. This file pins a build-time executable: the two name the same buildx version on purpose, and the recorder scores that agreement as a named comparison (`controlled_pin_vs_lock`) rather than merging one file into the other, so bumping one without the other is a finding about the repository instead of a silent divergence.
why_the_action_is_not_enough: docker/setup-buildx-action@8d2750c68a42422c14e847fe6c8ac0403b4cbd6f (v3.12.0) exposes the builder it created (outputs name/driver/platforms/nodes/endpoint/status/flags) but never exposes the buildx executable it installed: @docker/actions-toolkit's BuildxInstall.download() then installPlugin() copies the binary to $DOCKER_CONFIG/cli-plugins/docker-buildx and reports that path only in the job log. Batch 3A measured the consequence at five heads -- the same job text printed v0.37.0, v0.37.1 and v0.37.0 as the executing version, and `docker buildx version` printed no install path at all. So the requested version is not the executed version, and the executed version is not knowable from the CLI. The release jobs still run the action, because its `buildx-version` and `driver-opts` are one of the authorities `lock_vs_workflow` compares; what they no longer do is build through it.
install_contract: scripts/release/install_controlled_buildx.py is the one mechanism every job that builds a release image installs through: it refuses a docker CLI plugin target before downloading, fetches `source.download_url` to a .part file, checks the length against `source.asset_size_bytes` and the sha256 against `integrity.expected` (stopping there, before the bytes are chmod-ed, executed, or used to create a builder), moves it to `install.path`, reads `version` and the git commit back, checks the BuildKit reference against deployment/third-party-images.json, and only then creates the named builder with that executable. `build_release_image.sh` then runs `<install.path> build --builder <name>` and records the argv it used, and `record_build_producer.py` re-reads the executable, the builder, its container and the registry for itself.
expected_git_commit_derivation: github.com/docker/buildx annotated tag v0.37.1 -> tag object 363b7b083ea1a88098198d681f9d5054f1ca4629 -> tagged commit 0b265a9f62db554fa9aba6dd19e1bd5704bc7d8a (GET /repos/docker/buildx/git/refs/tags/v0.37.1 and /repos/docker/buildx/git/tags/363b7b08..., read 2026-09-23). A released buildx prints this commit in its version line, so it is a second, independent check on the bytes: the same version string built from a different commit would fail here rather than pass on a tag match.

integrity.expected_derivation: the `digest` GitHub records for release asset 557511570 (GET /repos/docker/buildx/releases/tags/v0.37.1, read 2026-09-23). It is pinned here rather than fetched at build time: a check that asks the same server the file came from would pass on any bytes that server later serves.
integrity.verified_by: sha256sum of the file at install.path, read back by the recorder as observed.controlled_buildx.integrity.computed

install.path_is_a_literal_on_purpose: configured.workflow must be a claim about the repository. A path assembled from ${{ runner.temp }} or $GITHUB_ENV exists only after the runner expands it, so the recorder would be comparing an expression instead of a pin. Each job declares this absolute path in its own env: block, and the installer refuses a target it does not match. Batch 3 A2.1 named the directory for the batch that introduced it; A2.2 renamed it to name the mechanism, because the release jobs install through it too.

relationship_to_the_release_lock: deployment/third-party-images.json names the same buildx version for the release path. This file must agree with it, and the recorder scores that agreement as a named field (configured.lock vs configured.controlled) rather than assuming it: if one file is bumped and the other is not, that is a finding about the repository, not a detail.
